observations.body: Samuel confronts Saul over spared spoil, asks whether sacrifice delights the LORD as much as obedience, and compares rebellion with divination.
observations.label: Obedience is better than sacrifice

observations.body: The passage presents command, spoil, religious rationale, hearing, rebellion, and rejection as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: command, spoil, religious rationale, hearing, rebellion, and rejection

observations.body: The passage places obedience critique beside command, spoil, religious rationale, hearing, rebellion, and rejection.

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 15:17–23 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the saying rejects sacrifice used against a command, not every sacrifice commanded elsewhere
payload.title: Obedience is better than sacrifice
